answer.generated: The purpose of an index in the context of database physical design is to improve query performance by facilitating faster data retrieval. An index serves as a data structure that speeds up data retrieval operations on a database by storing a sorted version of the key values along with pointers to the actual data locations. This allows the database management system (DBMS) to quickly locate the required data without scanning the entire table, thereby enhancing query efficiency and reducing response times.
